MGR1.claim: Shillong is 100 km from Guwahati on NH 40, about 2.5 hours.

evidence.quote: Shillong is just 100 km (62 mi) from Guwahati, accessible by road along NH 40.
The journey is of about 2 hours and 30 minutes

MGR2.claim: Shillong has no rail link; Umroi airport is about 30 km away; taxis run to Guwahati, Agartala, Kohima, Dimapur and Aizawl.

evidence.quote: Shillong is well-connected by road, but it neither has rail connections nor a proper air connection.
Shillong is served by the Shillong Airport, located about 30 km away in Umroi.
Taxi services are also available to destinations like Guwahati, Agartala, Kohima, Dimapur, Aizawl

MGR3.claim: Guwahati's airport is the primary airport of Northeast India.

evidence.quote: the primary airport of Northeast India

MGR4.claim: Cherrapunji (Sohra) is about 50 km from Shillong; Guwahati station, 165 km, is the nearest railhead; November–February is the drier season.

evidence.quote: The town is located around 50 kilometers from Shillong
Guwahati railway station, 165 km north, is the nearest railway station
The best time to visit Cherrapunjee is undoubtedly during winter, from November to February.

MGR5.claim: The trek to Nongriat's double-decker bridge starts at Tyrna and descends about 3,500 steps.

evidence.quote: This route begins from Tyrna village, involving a descent of about 3500 steps.

MGR6.claim: Meghalaya Tourism's 5-day route: Shillong city; Sohra's falls and caves; Nohkalikai and the descent to Nongriat; Pynursla's root bridges and Shnongpdeng; then Mawphlang Sacred Grove and Umiam Lake.

evidence.quote: Day 1: Shillong Explore key city sights around Shillong at a relaxed pace.
Day 3: Sohra → Nongriat Start early for Nongriat trek and waterfall views.
Day 4: Pynursla & Shnongpdeng Drive across ridges exploring root bridges and riverside village.
Day 5: Sacred Grove & Umiam Lake Gentle finish with sacred grove visit and lake views.

MGR7.claim: Day 2 stops: Mawkdok-Dympep viewpoint (optional zip-lining), Wah Kaba Falls, Arwah Caves and Dainthlen and Wei-Sawdong falls.

evidence.quote: Mawkdok‑Dympep Valley View Point Things to do : Photography, optional zip‑lining
Wah Kaba Waterfalls Things to do : View waterfall cascade into cliff gorge
Arwah Caves Things to do : Explore stalagmites, stalactites & fossils
Dainthlen & Wei‑Sawdong Falls Things to do : Descend to waterfalls, explore rock pools

MGR8.claim: At Mawphlang Sacred Grove take a guided forest walk; Umiam Lake has strolls and boating.

evidence.quote: Mawphlang Sacred Grove Things to do : Guided forest walk, learn Khasi traditions
Umiam Lake Things to do : Lake strolls, boating, lakeside photography

MGR9.claim: Dawki is about 80 km from Shillong on NH206 by shared taxi or cab; hire a private vehicle for Shnongpdeng; visit 6 am–6 pm; best October–May.

evidence.quote: From Shillong, travelers can reach Dawki by driving approximately 80 km along NH206.
For Shnongpdeng and Darang, hiring a private vehicle from Shillong is recommended for flexibility and comfort.
Visitors can visit Dawki between 6:00 AM and 6:00 PM.
The best time to visit Dawki is between October and May

MGR10.claim: Mawlynnong is about 76 km from Shillong; shared sumos run to Pynursla, then local cabs.

evidence.quote: Mawlynnong is located in the East Khasi Hills District, about 76 km from Shillong.
Shared sumos and taxis to Pynursla are available from Shillong

MGR11.claim: Umiam Lake is 15 km north of Shillong.

evidence.quote: is a reservoir in the hills 15 km (9.3 mi) north of Shillong

MGR12.claim: Book authorised cabs from hotels, avoid isolated areas without a guide, drink bottled water and dress conservatively.

evidence.quote: If possible, book authorized cabs from hotels; avoid unidentified or unnumbered vehicles.
Avoid isolated areas without a guide.
Use bottled water and eat at established restaurants
Dress comfortably but conservatively.

MGR13.claim: Spring is March–April; the monsoon May–September; post-monsoon October–November is harvest-festival time; winter November–February is driest and best for caves.

evidence.quote: A Pleasant Spring Escape – March and April
The Mega Monsoons – May to September
The post-monsoon is the harvest season so it is also the time when a lot of traditional festivals are happening across the state
It is also the best time for those who want to explore the many caves in the state.

MGR14.claim: Swimming and water activities are not permitted in most areas during the monsoon; watch for heavy-rain and landslide warnings.

evidence.quote: swimming and other water activities are not permitted in most areas for (obvious) safety reasons
pay attention to warnings of heavy rains and landslides

MGR15.claim: Winter is the driest season; some highland areas see sub-zero early mornings; pack warm and book stays ahead.

evidence.quote: The wintertime is the driest season of the year
experience sub-zero temperatures in the early mornings
Book your accommodations in advance, as winter is a busy season for tourists.

MGR16.claim: In the monsoon pack a waterproof jacket, umbrella and anti-slip shoes; weather is unpredictable at any time of year.

evidence.quote: Pack for rain – waterproof bag, waterproof jacket, umbrella, anti-slip shoes, quick-drying clothes.
Experiencing all seasons in a single day is a real possibility!

MGR17.claim: Mawsynram is 61 km from Shillong; MTDC runs guided day trips by car.

evidence.quote: From Shillong: drive 61 km via East Khasi Hills; shared taxis or private cars are common.
Guided day trips (car only, no buses) are available through MTDC circuits.

MGR18.claim: Kongthong is 55–60 km from Shillong by shared sumo or taxi; best October–April.

evidence.quote: The nearest city is Shillong, which is approximately 55-60 km away.
The best time to visit is from October to April

MGR19.claim: Jowai is 64 km from Shillong; shared Tata Sumos are the main transport.

evidence.quote: Jowai is well connected by roadways to Shillong, which is 64 km away.
The district's most popular modes of transport are the Tata Sumo and the Tata Indica, which function on a shared passenger basis.

MGR20.claim: Khasi dishes to try include doh neiiong (pork in black-sesame gravy) and tungrymbai (fermented soybean).

evidence.quote: pork cooked in velvety gravy made of black sesame seeds
Tungrymbai, a delicious Meghalayan delicacy prepared from fermented soybeans

itineraries.title: Meghalaya in 5 days: Sohra, Nongriat, Shnongpdeng and Mawphlang
itineraries.summary: Meghalaya Tourism's own 5-day Khasi Hills route: Shillong, Sohra's falls and caves, a night in Nongriat by the double-decker root bridge, the Umngot at Shnongpdeng, and Mawphlang's sacred grove.
itineraries.seoDescription: Five days in Meghalaya following the official route: Shillong, Sohra's waterfalls and caves, the Nongriat root bridge, Shnongpdeng on the Umngot and Mawphlang.

plan.overview: This follows Meghalaya Tourism's suggested 5-day route through the Khasi Hills. It moves on almost every day — Shillong, Sohra, a night down in Nongriat by the root bridges, the clear Umngot river at Shnongpdeng, and an easy last morning at Mawphlang and Umiam Lake before Guwahati. Go October to May: the Umngot is clearest then and Sohra is drier from November to February.
plan.season: October–May (Dawki's season); November–February is driest in Sohra
plan.difficulty: Moderate — one long descent to Nongriat (about 3,500 steps)
plan.transport: Hired taxi; on foot to Nongriat. A private vehicle is recommended for Shnongpdeng.

days.title: Guwahati to Shillong
days.summary: Drive up to Shillong and see the city at an easy pace: Ward's Lake, the Cathedral, and Elephant Falls.

stops.name: Elephant Falls
stops.note: A two-tier fall on the city's edge.

days.meals: Dinner in Shillong: try doh neiiong and tungrymbai.

days.title: Sohra's viewpoints, falls and caves
days.summary: South to Sohra: Mawkdok-Dympep valley view, Wah Kaba Falls, Arwah Caves, and the Dainthlen and Wei-Sawdong falls.
days.travel: Shillong to Sohra is about 50 km.
days.meals: Lunch near Sohra; dinner at your guesthouse.

days.title: Nohkalikai and down to Nongriat
days.summary: Morning at Nohkalikai, then the long descent from Tyrna to Nongriat — sleep in the village by the double-decker root bridge.
days.travel: Short drive to Tyrna, then on foot.
days.logistics: Pack light — everything goes down and back up the steps.

days.title: Up from Nongriat to Pynursla and Shnongpdeng
days.summary: Climb back to Tyrna, then drive across the ridges to Pynursla's root bridges and down to the Umngot at Shnongpdeng.

stops.name: Shnongpdeng on the Umngot
stops.note: Clearest water in the afternoon; boating and kayaking.

days.travel: Hire a private vehicle; Dawki is about 80 km from Shillong along NH206.
days.access: Dawki is open to visitors 6 am–6 pm

days.title: Mawphlang, Umiam Lake and back to Guwahati
days.summary: A guided walk in Mawphlang Sacred Grove, a stop at Umiam Lake, then down to Guwahati.

stops.name: Mawphlang Sacred Grove
stops.note: Go with a guide to learn the Khasi traditions.

days.travel: Via Shillong to Guwahati (100 km, about 2.5 hours from Shillong).

budget.assumptions: Meghalaya Tourism doesn't publish prices for this route. VacayOut hasn't checked taxi, homestay, camp or guide prices.

booking.detail: Guwahati is the primary airport of Northeast India.
Book authorised cabs through your hotel; hire a private vehicle for Shnongpdeng.
Meghalaya Tourism's helpline, 1800 599 2026, helps with itineraries, transport and stays.

alternatives: Not up for the Nongriat night: do the trek as a day from Sohra and stay in Sohra both nights.
Add Mawlynnong (about 76 km from Shillong) on day 4 on the way to the Umngot.
In the monsoon swap the river day for falls — swimming and water activities are not permitted in most areas then.
tips: The Umngot looks clearest in the afternoon light.
Keep a light jacket — the weather can change within a day.

prep.title: Season
prep.body: Spring is March–April, the monsoon May–September, post-monsoon October–November (harvest festivals) and winter November–February, the driest and best for caves. Dawki's season runs October to May.

prep.title: Safety
prep.body: Book authorised cabs, avoid isolated areas without a guide, drink bottled water and dress conservatively. In the monsoon, check heavy-rain and landslide warnings.

faqs.q: Is this route from Meghalaya Tourism?
faqs.a: Yes — it follows the state tourism department's suggested 5-day itinerary, with drive distances added.

faqs.q: How far is Dawki from Shillong?

faqs.a: Yes, in simple village homestays; staying lets you see the bridges without rushing back up the 3,500 steps.

guides.title: How to reach and get around Meghalaya
guides.summary: Fly to Guwahati or Shillong's Umroi airport, then by road to Shillong; shared sumos, taxis and MTDC day trips onward, with distances from Shillong to Sohra, Dawki, Mawlynnong, Mawsynram, Kongthong and Jowai.
guides.seoTitle: How to Reach Meghalaya & Get Around: Shillong, Sohra, Dawki
guides.seoDescription: Getting to Meghalaya and around it: Guwahati and Umroi airports, the road to Shillong, shared sumos and taxis, and distances from Shillong to the main sights.

body.intro: Meghalaya has no working railway, so almost everyone arrives by road from Guwahati or flies into Shillong's small Umroi airport. Shillong is the hub: shared sumos and taxis fan out from there to Sohra, the Umngot river, the root-bridge villages and the Jaintia Hills.

items.title: Guwahati
items.body: Guwahati's airport is the primary airport of Northeast India, and Guwahati station is the nearest railhead (165 km from Sohra). Shillong is 100 km away on NH 40, about 2.5 hours.

items.title: Shillong airport
items.body: Shillong's airport is at Umroi, about 30 km from the city.

items.title: By taxi
items.body: Taxis run from Shillong to Guwahati, Agartala, Kohima, Dimapur and Aizawl.

items.title: Kongthong
items.body: About 55–60 km by shared sumo or taxi, then a short walk.

items.title: Mawsynram
items.body: 61 km; MTDC runs guided day trips by car.

items.title: Jowai
items.body: 64 km; shared Tata Sumos are the main transport.

items.title: Mawlynnong
items.body: About 76 km; shared sumos to Pynursla, then a local cab.

items.title: Dawki
items.body: About 80 km along NH206 by shared taxi or cab; hire a private vehicle for Shnongpdeng.

sections.heading: Getting around safely
sections.text: Book authorised cabs through your hotel and avoid unidentified or unnumbered vehicles. Avoid isolated areas without a guide, drink bottled water and eat at established restaurants.

checklist: Fly into Guwahati (or Umroi for Shillong).
Book an authorised taxi for the hills.
Keep the Meghalaya Tourism helpline, 1800 599 2026, handy.

guides.title: Best time to visit Meghalaya: season by season
guides.summary: Spring for escaping the heat, the monsoon for the falls, post-monsoon for festivals and winter for dry trails and caves — plus what to pack and when Sohra, Dawki and Kongthong are at their best.
guides.seoTitle: Best Time to Visit Meghalaya: Season-by-Season Guide
guides.seoDescription: When to visit Meghalaya: spring, monsoon, post-monsoon and winter, what to pack, and the best months for Sohra, Dawki, Mawsynram and Kongthong.

body.intro: Meghalaya rises from near sea level to almost 2,000 m and is one of the wettest places on Earth, so the season changes the trip completely. Meghalaya Tourism splits the year into four seasons.

items.title: Spring — March and April
items.body: Nippy evenings in the highlands and plenty of sunny days; a light jacket is enough.

items.title: Monsoon — May to September
items.body: The falls and rivers are at full flow; swimming and water activities are not permitted in most areas.

items.title: Post-monsoon — October and November
items.body: Clearer skies and harvest festivals across the state.

items.title: Winter — November to February
items.body: The driest, sunniest season — best for hikes, camping and caves; some highland areas see sub-zero early mornings.

items.title: Sohra (Cherrapunji)
items.body: November to February, the drier season.

items.title: Mawsynram
items.body: Post-monsoon and winter for clearer trails.

sections.heading: What to pack
sections.text: Monsoon: a waterproof bag and jacket, umbrella, anti-slip shoes and quick-drying clothes, and watch for heavy-rain and landslide warnings. Winter: thermals, jackets, gloves and socks — and book stays ahead, as winter is busy. Whatever the month, keep a sweater handy: you can get all seasons in a single day.

checklist: Pick your season by what you want: falls (monsoon) or dry trails (winter).
